מְלַמֵּ֥ד יָדַ֖י לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְנִחַ֥ת קֶֽשֶׁת־נְחוּשָׁ֖ה זְרֹעֹתָֽי׃
You have given me the shield of your salvation; your help[^24] has made me great.
וַתִּתֶּן־לִ֖י מָגֵ֣ן יִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וַעֲנֹתְךָ֖ תַּרְבֵּֽנִי׃
You make a wide place for my steps beneath me, and my ankles have not slipped.
תַּרְחִ֥יב צַעֲדִ֖י תַּחְתֵּ֑נִי וְלֹ֥א מָעֲד֖וּ קַרְסֻלָּֽי׃
I pursued my enemies and destroyed them; I did not turn back until they were finished off.
אֶרְדְּפָ֥ה אֹיְבַ֖י וָאַשְׁמִידֵ֑ם וְלֹ֥א אָשׁ֖וּב עַד־כַּלּוֹתָֽם׃
I finished them off and crushed them, so that they could not rise; they fell beneath my feet.
וָאֲכַלֵּ֥ם וָאֶמְחָצֵ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יְקוּמ֑וּן וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ תַּ֥חַת רַגְלָֽי׃
You armed me with strength for battle; you made those who rose against me bow down beneath me.
וַתַּזְרֵ֥נִי חַ֖יִל לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה תַּכְרִ֥יעַ קָמַ֖י תַּחְתֵּֽנִי׃
You made my enemies turn their backs to me;[^25] those who hated me, I destroyed them.
וְאֹ֣יְבַ֔י תַּ֥תָּה לִּ֖י עֹ֑רֶף מְשַׂנְאַ֖י וָאַצְמִיתֵֽם׃
They looked for help,[^26] but there was no one to save them; they looked to the LORD, but he did not answer them.
יִשְׁע֖וּ וְאֵ֣ין מֹשִׁ֑יעַ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א עָנָֽם׃
I beat them as fine as the dust of the earth; I crushed them and trampled them like the mud of the streets.
וְאֶשְׁחָקֵ֖ם כַּעֲפַר־אָ֑רֶץ כְּטִיט־חוּצ֥וֹת אֲדִקֵּ֖ם אֶרְקָעֵֽם׃
You rescued me from the strife of my people; you kept me as the head of nations. A people I did not know now serve me.
וַֽתְּפַלְּטֵ֔נִי מֵרִיבֵ֖י עַמִּ֑י תִּשְׁמְרֵ֙נִי֙ לְרֹ֣אשׁ גּוֹיִ֔ם עַ֥ם לֹא־יָדַ֖עְתִּי יַעַבְדֻֽנִי׃
Foreigners come cringing to me;[^27] as soon as they hear of me, they obey me.
בְּנֵ֥י נֵכָ֖ר יִתְכַּֽחֲשׁוּ־לִ֑י לִשְׁמ֥וֹעַ אֹ֖זֶן יִשָּׁ֥מְעוּ לִֽי׃
Foreigners lose heart, and they come limping[^28] out of their strongholds.
בְּנֵ֥י נֵכָ֖ר יִבֹּ֑לוּ וְיַחְגְּר֖וּ מִמִּסְגְּרוֹתָֽם׃
The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,
חַי־יְהוָ֖ה וּבָר֣וּךְ צוּרִ֑י וְיָרֻ֕ם אֱלֹהֵ֖י צ֥וּר יִשְׁעִֽי׃
the God who grants me vengeance and brings peoples down under me,
הָאֵ֕ל הַנֹּתֵ֥ן נְקָמֹ֖ת לִ֑י וּמוֹרִ֥יד עַמִּ֖ים תַּחְתֵּֽנִי׃
who brings me out from my enemies. You lift me high above those who rise against me; you rescue me from violent men.
וּמוֹצִיאִ֖י מֵאֹֽיְבָ֑י וּמִקָּמַי֙ תְּר֣וֹמְמֵ֔נִי מֵאִ֥ישׁ חֲמָסִ֖ים תַּצִּילֵֽנִי׃
So I will praise you, LORD, among the nations, and sing praises to your name.[^29]
עַל־כֵּ֛ן אוֹדְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם וּלְשִׁמְךָ֖ אֲזַמֵּֽר׃
He is a tower of salvation[^30] for his king; he shows faithful love[^31] to his anointed,[^32] to David and his offspring forever.
*מגדיל **מִגְדּ֖וֹל יְשׁוּע֣וֹת מַלְכּ֑וֹ וְעֹֽשֶׂה־חֶ֧סֶד לִמְשִׁיח֛וֹ לְדָוִ֥ד וּלְזַרְע֖וֹ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃ פ

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: This song appears again, with small differences, as Psalm 18. From verse 4 on, its verse numbers match those of Psalm 18 in the Hebrew; in English Bibles the psalm's verses are numbered one lower. The notes below give some of the differences.
n.3: Psalm 18 begins "I love you, LORD, my strength" (18:2) before these words.
n.4: Literally "the God of my rock". Psalm 18:3 has "my God, my rock".
n.5: A symbol of strength, like the horns of a wild ox.
n.6: Psalm 18:3 does not have "and my refuge; my savior, you save me from violence".
n.7: Psalm 18:5 has "the cords of death".
n.8: Hebrew *beliyya'al*, "worthlessness", here perhaps destruction or the realm of death.
n.9: Hebrew *Sheol*: the realm of the dead.
n.10: Psalm 18:8 has "the foundations of the mountains".
n.11: Hebrew *keruv*, one of the winged heavenly beings (see 6:2).
n.12: Hebrew *vayyera*. Psalm 18:11 and many Hebrew manuscripts of Samuel read *vayyede*, "he swooped", which differs by one similar letter.
n.13: Hebrew *chashrat mayim*, a phrase found only here, perhaps "a gathering of waters". Psalm 18:12 has "dark waters".
n.14: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.15: The Hebrew text is written "his ruling" but read "his rulings".
n.16: Literally "and his decrees, I do not turn aside from it".
n.18: Hebrew *chasid*, "faithful, loyal", and the verb from the same root, related to *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.19: Or "I can run through a barricade".
n.20: That is, tested and pure, like metal refined in a furnace.
n.21: Literally "God is my refuge of strength". Psalm 18:33 has "the God who arms me with strength".
n.22: Literally "and he sets free blameless my way". The meaning of the verb is uncertain. The Hebrew text is written "his way" but read "my way". Psalm 18:33 has "and makes my way blameless".
n.23: The Hebrew text is written "his feet" but read "my feet".
n.24: Hebrew *anotkha*, perhaps "your answering" or "your help". Psalm 18:36 has "your gentleness" and adds "your right hand supports me".
n.25: Literally "My enemies, you gave me their neck."
n.26: Hebrew *yish'u*, "they looked". Psalm 18:42 has "they cried for help".
n.28: Hebrew *yachgeru*, perhaps "limp", or "gird themselves". Psalm 18:46 has "come trembling".
n.29: Psalm 18:50 (18:49 in most English Bibles) is quoted in Romans 15:9.
n.30: The Hebrew text is written "He gives great victories", as in Psalm 18:51, but read "He is a tower of salvation".
n.32: Hebrew *meshicho*, "his anointed one", the king anointed at the LORD's command.

v: These are the last words of David: The declaration[^1] of David son of Jesse, the declaration of the man who was raised on high,[^2] the anointed of the God of Jacob, the sweet singer of the songs of Israel:[^3]
וְאֵ֛לֶּה דִּבְרֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד הָאַֽחֲרֹנִ֑ים נְאֻ֧ם דָּוִ֣ד בֶּן־יִשַׁ֗י וּנְאֻ֤ם הַגֶּ֙בֶר֙ הֻ֣קַם עָ֔ל מְשִׁ֙יחַ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּנְעִ֖ים זְמִר֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
The Spirit of the LORD[^4] spoke through me; his word was on my tongue.
ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֶּר־בִּ֑י וּמִלָּת֖וֹ עַל־לְשׁוֹנִֽי׃
The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me: "One who rules over people in righteousness, who rules in the fear of God,
אָמַר֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִ֥י דִבֶּ֖ר צ֣וּר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מוֹשֵׁל֙ בָּאָדָ֔ם צַדִּ֕יק מוֹשֵׁ֖ל יִרְאַ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים׃
is like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, when the grass springs from the earth through sunshine after rain."[^5]
וּכְא֥וֹר בֹּ֖קֶר יִזְרַח־שָׁ֑מֶשׁ בֹּ֚קֶר לֹ֣א עָב֔וֹת מִנֹּ֥גַהּ מִמָּטָ֖ר דֶּ֥שֶׁא מֵאָֽרֶץ׃
Is not my house like this with God?[^6] For he has made an everlasting covenant with me, ordered in every part and secured. Will he not make all my salvation and all my desire grow?
כִּֽי־לֹא־כֵ֥ן בֵּיתִ֖י עִם־אֵ֑ל כּ[c]י֩ בְרִ֨ית עוֹלָ֜ם שָׂ֣ם לִ֗י עֲרוּכָ֤ה בַכֹּל֙ וּשְׁמֻרָ֔ה כִּֽי־כָל־יִשְׁעִ֥י וְכָל־חֵ֖פֶץ כִּֽי־לֹ֥א יַצְמִֽיחַ׃
But the worthless[^7] are all like thorns that are tossed away, for they cannot be picked up by hand.
וּבְלִיַּ֕עַל כְּק֥וֹץ מֻנָ֖ד כֻּלָּ֑הַם כִּֽי־לֹ֥א בְיָ֖ד יִקָּֽחוּ׃
Whoever touches them must arm himself with iron or the shaft of a spear, and they are utterly burned up with fire where they lie.[^8]
וְאִישׁ֙ יִגַּ֣ע בָּהֶ֔ם יִמָּלֵ֥א בַרְזֶ֖ל וְעֵ֣ץ חֲנִ֑ית וּבָאֵ֕שׁ שָׂר֥וֹף יִשָּׂרְפ֖וּ בַּשָּֽׁבֶת׃ פ
These are the names of David's mighty warriors: Josheb-basshebeth[^9] the Tahchemonite, the chief of the officers.[^10] He was Adino the Eznite, who killed eight hundred men at one time.[^11]
אֵ֛לֶּה שְׁמ֥וֹת הַגִּבֹּרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑ד יֹשֵׁ֨ב בַּשֶּׁ֜בֶת תַּחְכְּמֹנִ֣י ׀ רֹ֣אשׁ הַשָּׁלִשִׁ֗י ה֚וּא עֲדִינ֣וֹ *העצנו **הָֽעֶצְנִ֔י עַל־שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֛וֹת חָלָ֖ל בְּפַ֥עַם *אחד **אֶחָֽת׃ ס

Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodo,[^12] son of Ahohi,[^13] one of the three mighty warriors with David when they taunted the Philistines who were gathered there for battle. The men of Israel withdrew,

*ואחרו **וְאַחֲרָ֛יו אֶלְעָזָ֥ר בֶּן־*דדי **דֹּד֖וֹ בֶּן־אֲחֹחִ֑י בִּשְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה *גברים **הַגִּבֹּרִ֜ים עִם־דָּוִ֗ד בְּחָֽרְפָ֤ם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ נֶאֶסְפוּ־שָׁ֣ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

but he stood his ground and struck down the Philistines until his hand grew tired and stuck to the sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day, and the troops came back after him only to strip the dead.

ה֣וּא קָם֩ וַיַּ֨ךְ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֜ים עַ֣ד ׀ כִּֽי־יָגְעָ֣ה יָד֗וֹ וַתִּדְבַּ֤ק יָדוֹ֙ אֶל־הַחֶ֔רֶב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוָ֛ה תְּשׁוּעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְהָעָ֛ם יָשֻׁ֥בוּ אַחֲרָ֖יו אַךְ־לְפַשֵּֽׁט׃ ס
Next to him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines had gathered together at Lehi,[^14] where there was a plot of ground full of lentils, and the troops fled from the Philistines.
וְאַחֲרָ֛יו שַׁמָּ֥א בֶן־אָגֵ֖א הָרָרִ֑י וַיֵּאָסְפ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים לַחַיָּ֗ה וַתְּהִי־שָׁ֞ם חֶלְקַ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ מְלֵאָ֣ה עֲדָשִׁ֔ים וְהָעָ֥ם נָ֖ס מִפְּנֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
But he took his stand in the middle of the plot, defended it and struck down the Philistines. And the LORD brought about a great victory.
וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֤ב בְּתוֹךְ־הַֽחֶלְקָה֙ וַיַּצִּילֶ֔הָ וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יְהוָ֖ה תְּשׁוּעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃ ס
Three[^15] of the Thirty,[^16] the chiefs, went down at harvest time[^17] and came to David at the cave of Adullam, while a band of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
וַיֵּרְד֨וּ *שלשים **שְׁלֹשָׁ֜ה מֵהַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֣ים רֹ֗אשׁ וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ אֶל־קָצִיר֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד אֶל־מְעָרַ֖ת עֲדֻלָּ֑ם וְחַיַּ֣ת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים חֹנָ֖ה בְּעֵ֥מֶק רְפָאִֽים׃
At that time David was in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison was then at Bethlehem.
וְדָוִ֖ד אָ֣ז בַּמְּצוּדָ֑ה וּמַצַּ֣ב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אָ֖ז בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃
David felt a craving and said, "If only someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate!"
וַיִּתְאַוֶּ֥ה דָוִ֖ד וַיֹּאמַ֑ר מִ֚י יַשְׁקֵ֣נִי מַ֔יִם מִבֹּ֥אר בֵּֽית־לֶ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁעַר׃

So the three mighty warriors broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, and carried it back to David. But he would not drink it. He poured it out to the LORD

וַיִּבְקְעוּ֩ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת הַגִּבֹּרִ֜ים בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיִּֽשְׁאֲבוּ־מַ֙יִם֙ מִבֹּ֤אר בֵּֽית־לֶ֙חֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשַּׁ֔עַר וַיִּשְׂא֖וּ וַיָּבִ֣אוּ אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד וְלֹ֤א אָבָה֙ לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֔ם וַיַּסֵּ֥ךְ אֹתָ֖ם לַֽיהוָֽה׃

and said, "Far be it from me, LORD, that I should do this! Is it not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?"[^18] So he would not drink it. These were the deeds of the three mighty warriors.
וַיֹּ֡אמֶר חָלִילָה֩ לִּ֨י יְהוָ֜ה מֵעֲשֹׂ֣תִי זֹ֗את הֲדַ֤ם הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בְּנַפְשׁוֹתָ֔ם וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֑ם אֵ֣לֶּה עָשׂ֔וּ שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת הַגִּבֹּרִֽים׃ ס
Abishai, the brother of Joab son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three.[^19] He wielded his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and he won a name among the Three.
וַאֲבִישַׁ֞י אֲחִ֣י ׀ יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֗ה ה֚וּא רֹ֣אשׁ *השלשי **הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְהוּא֙ עוֹרֵ֣ר אֶת־חֲנִית֔וֹ עַל־שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת חָלָ֑ל וְלוֹ־שֵׁ֖ם בַּשְּׁלֹשָֽׁה׃
Was he not the most honored of the Three?[^20] He became their commander, but he did not attain to the Three.
מִן־הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה֙ הֲכִ֣י נִכְבָּ֔ד וַיְהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לְשָׂ֑ר וְעַד־הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֖ה לֹא־בָֽא׃ ס

Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a valiant man[^21] from Kabzeel, a man of great deeds. He struck down two champions[^22] of Moab. He also went down and killed a lion inside a pit on a snowy day.

וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֧ע בֶּן־אִֽישׁ־*חי **חַ֛יִל רַב־פְּעָלִ֖ים מִֽקַּבְצְאֵ֑ל ה֣וּא הִכָּ֗ה אֵ֣ת שְׁנֵ֤י אֲרִאֵל֙ מוֹאָ֔ב וְ֠הוּא יָרַ֞ד וְהִכָּ֧ה אֶֽת־*האריה **הָאֲרִ֛י בְּת֥וֹךְ הַבֹּ֖אר בְּי֥וֹם הַשָּֽׁלֶג׃

He also struck down an Egyptian, a man of impressive appearance. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a club, snatched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
וְהוּא־הִכָּה֩ אֶת־אִ֨ישׁ מִצְרִ֜י *אשר **אִ֣ישׁ מַרְאֶ֗ה וּבְיַ֤ד הַמִּצְרִי֙ חֲנִ֔ית וַיֵּ֥רֶד אֵלָ֖יו בַּשָּׁ֑בֶט וַיִּגְזֹ֤ל אֶֽת־הַחֲנִית֙ מִיַּ֣ד הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַיַּהַרְגֵ֖הוּ בַּחֲנִיתֽוֹ׃
These were the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he won a name among the three mighty warriors.
אֵ֣לֶּה עָשָׂ֔ה בְּנָיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע וְלוֹ־שֵׁ֖ם בִּשְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה הַגִּבֹּרִֽים׃
He was more honored than the Thirty, but he did not attain to the Three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.[^23]
מִן־הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֣ים נִכְבָּ֔ד וְאֶל־הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֖ה לֹא־בָ֑א וַיְשִׂמֵ֥הוּ דָוִ֖ד אֶל־מִשְׁמַעְתּֽוֹ׃ ס
Among the Thirty were Asahel the brother of Joab; Elhanan son of Dodo, of Bethlehem;
עֲשָׂה־אֵ֥ל אֲחִֽי־יוֹאָ֖ב בַּשְּׁלֹשִׁ֑ים אֶלְחָנָ֥ן בֶּן־דֹּד֖וֹ בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃
Shammah the Harodite; Elika the Harodite;
שַׁמָּה֙ הַֽחֲרֹדִ֔י אֱלִיקָ֖א הַחֲרֹדִֽי׃ ס
Helez the Paltite; Ira son of Ikkesh, the Tekoite;
חֶ֚לֶץ הַפַּלְטִ֔י עִירָ֥א בֶן־עִקֵּ֖שׁ הַתְּקוֹעִֽי׃ ס
Abiezer the Anathothite; Mebunnai[^24] the Hushathite;
אֲבִיעֶ֙זֶר֙ הָֽעֲ[c]נְּתֹתִ֔י מְבֻנַּ֖י הַחֻשָׁתִֽי׃ ס
Zalmon the Ahohite; Maharai the Netophathite;
צַלְמוֹן֙ הָֽאֲחֹחִ֔י מַהְרַ֖י הַנְּטֹפָתִֽי׃ ס
Heleb[^25] son of Baanah, the Netophathite; Ittai son of Ribai, from Gibeah of the Benjaminites;
חֵ֥לֶב בֶּֽן־בַּעֲנָ֖ה הַנְּטֹפָתִ֑י ס אִתַּי֙ בֶּן־רִיבַ֔י מִגִּבְעַ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִֽן׃ ס
Benaiah the Pirathonite; Hiddai of the ravines of Gaash;
בְּנָיָ֙הוּ֙ פִּרְעָ֣תֹנִ֔י הִדַּ֖י מִנַּ֥חֲלֵי גָֽעַשׁ׃ ס
Abi-albon the Arbathite; Azmaveth the Barhumite;
אֲבִֽי־עַלְבוֹן֙ הָֽעַרְבָתִ֔י עַזְמָ֖וֶת הַבַּרְחֻמִֽי׃ ס
Eliahba the Shaalbonite; the sons of Jashen; Jonathan;[^26]
אֶלְיַחְבָּא֙ הַשַּׁ֣עַלְבֹנִ֔י בְּנֵ֥י יָשֵׁ֖ן יְהוֹנָתָֽן׃ ס
Shammah the Hararite; Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite;[^27]
שַׁמָּה֙ הַֽהֲרָרִ֔י אֲחִיאָ֥ם בֶּן־שָׁרָ֖ר הָארָרִֽי׃ ס
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maacathite; Eliam son of Ahithophel, the Gilonite;
אֱלִיפֶ֥לֶט בֶּן־אֲחַסְבַּ֖י בֶּן־הַמַּֽעֲכָתִ֑י ס אֱלִיעָ֥ם בֶּן־אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל הַגִּלֹנִֽי׃ ס
Hezrai[^28] the Carmelite; Paarai the Arbite;
*חצרו **חֶצְרַי֙ הַֽכַּרְמְלִ֔י פַּעֲרַ֖י הָאַרְבִּֽי׃ ס
Igal son of Nathan, from Zobah; Bani the Gadite;
יִגְאָ֤ל בֶּן־נָתָן֙ מִצֹּבָ֔ה ס בָּנִ֖י הַגָּדִֽי׃ ס
Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer[^29] of Joab son of Zeruiah;
צֶ֖לֶק הָעַמֹּנִ֑י ס נַחְרַי֙ הַבְּאֵ֣רֹתִ֔י *נשאי **נֹשֵׂ֕א כְּלֵ֖י יוֹאָ֥ב בֶּן־צְרֻיָֽה׃ ס
Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
עִירָא֙ הַיִּתְרִ֔י גָּרֵ֖ב הַיִּתְרִֽי׃ ס
and Uriah the Hittite. Thirty-seven in all.
אֽוּרִיָּה֙ הַֽחִתִּ֔י כֹּ֖ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָֽה׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *ne'um*, a word often used of a prophet's message: "declaration, oracle".
n.2: Hebrew *huqam al*, "raised up on high". 4QSam(a), a Dead Sea Scroll of Samuel, reads "whom God raised up".
n.3: Literally "the pleasant one of the songs of Israel". Or "the favorite of the Strong One of Israel", taking *zemirot* in the sense "strength".
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: Literally "and like the light of morning the sun rises, a morning without clouds; from brightness, from rain, grass from the earth".
n.6: Or "Truly my house is not so with God."
n.7: Hebrew *beliyya'al*, "worthlessness": the wicked.
n.8: Literally "in the sitting", perhaps meaning "on the spot".
n.9: Hebrew *yoshev ba-shevet*, "one who sits in the seat", probably a damaged form of the name. 1 Chronicles 11:11 has "Jashobeam", and some manuscripts of the Septuagint have "Ishbosheth".
n.10: Hebrew *ha-shalishi*, perhaps "the officers" (literally "third men", perhaps the third man in a chariot). Many take it as "the Three" (verses 18–23).
n.11: The Hebrew of this sentence is difficult. Literally "He, Adino the Eznite, over eight hundred slain at one time." The Hebrew text is written *ha-etsno* but read *ha-etsni*, "the Eznite". 1 Chronicles 11:11 reads "He wielded his spear against three hundred, whom he killed at one time" (compare verse 18).
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "Dodai" but read "Dodo".
n.13: Or "the Ahohite", as in 1 Chronicles 11:12 (compare verse 28).
n.14: Hebrew *la-chayyah*, "into a troop", or "at Lehi" (Judges 15:9). The same word is translated "band" in verse 13.
n.15: The Hebrew text is written "Thirty" but read "Three".
n.16: David's elite company of warriors, whose names are listed in verses 24–39.
n.17: Hebrew *el qatsir*, "to the harvest". 1 Chronicles 11:15 has "to the rock".
n.18: Literally "The blood of the men who went with their lives?" 1 Chronicles 11:19 reads "Shall I drink the blood of these men, who went at the risk of their lives?"
n.19: The Hebrew text is written *ha-shelishi*, which may mean "the officers" (as in verse 8), but read "the Three". Also in verse 19.
n.20: Literally "Of the Three, was he not honored?" Since in the second half of the verse Abishai does not attain to the Three, many think "the Thirty" is meant, as in verse 23.
n.21: The Hebrew text is written "a living man" but read "a valiant man".
n.22: Hebrew *ari'el*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "champion". The Septuagint reads "the two sons of Ariel of Moab".
n.23: Hebrew *mishma'ato*, literally "those who obey him", perhaps his personal guard or council.
n.24: Called Sibbecai in 21:18 and in 1 Chronicles 11:29.
n.26: The Hebrew is probably damaged. 1 Chronicles 11:34 reads "the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite".
n.27: Hebrew *ha-arari*, probably another spelling of *ha-harari*, "the Hararite".
n.28: The Hebrew text is written "Hezro" but read "Hezrai".
n.29: The Hebrew text is written "the armor-bearers" but read "the armor-bearer".

v: Again the anger of the LORD[^1] burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, "Go, count Israel and Judah."[^2]
וַיֹּ֙סֶף֙ אַף־יְהוָ֔ה לַחֲר֖וֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֨סֶת אֶת־דָּוִ֤ד בָּהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֵ֛ךְ מְנֵ֥ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶת־יְהוּדָֽה׃

So the king said to Joab, the commander of the army, who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and register the people, so that I may know the number of the people."
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־יוֹאָ֣ב ׀ שַׂר־הַחַ֣יִל אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֗וֹ שֽׁוּט־נָ֞א בְּכָל־שִׁבְטֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִדָּן֙ וְעַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע וּפִקְד֖וּ אֶת־הָעָ֑ם וְיָ֣דַעְתִּ֔י אֵ֖ת מִסְפַּ֥ר הָעָֽם׃ ס
Joab said to the king, "May the LORD your God multiply the people a hundred times over, while the eyes of my lord the king can still see it! But why does my lord the king want to do this?"

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹאָ֜ב אֶל־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְיוֹסֵ֣ף יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ אֶל־הָעָ֜ם כָּהֵ֤ם ׀ וְכָהֵם֙ מֵאָ֣ה פְעָמִ֔ים וְעֵינֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ רֹא֑וֹת וַאדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֥מָּה חָפֵ֖ץ בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
But the king's word prevailed against Joab and the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army went out from the king's presence to register the people of Israel.
וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק דְּבַר־הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־יוֹאָ֔ב וְעַ֖ל שָׂרֵ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וַיֵּצֵ֨א יוֹאָ֜ב וְשָׂרֵ֤י הַחַ֙יִל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לִפְקֹ֥ד אֶת־הָעָ֖ם אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
They crossed the Jordan and camped at Aroer, south of the town that is in the middle of the valley,[^3] toward Gad and on to Jazer.
וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בַעֲרוֹעֵ֗ר יְמִ֥ין הָעִ֛יר אֲשֶׁ֛ר בְּתוֹךְ־הַנַּ֥חַל הַגָּ֖ד וְאֶל־יַעְזֵֽר׃
Then they came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi,[^4] and they came to Dan-jaan[^5] and around toward Sidon.
וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ הַגִּלְעָ֔דָה וְאֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ תַּחְתִּ֖ים חָדְשִׁ֑י וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ דָּ֣נָה יַּ֔עַן וְסָבִ֖יב אֶל־צִידֽוֹן׃
They came to the fortress of Tyre and to all the towns of the Hivites and the Canaanites, and they went out to the Negev of Judah at Beersheba.
וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ מִבְצַר־צֹ֔ר וְכָל־עָרֵ֥י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י וַיּ[t]ֵֽ[m]צְא֛וּ אֶל־נֶ֥גֶב יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃
So they went through the whole land, and at the end of nine months and twenty days they came back to Jerusalem.
וַיָּשֻׁ֖טוּ בְּכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ מִקְצֵ֨ה תִשְׁעָ֧ה חֳדָשִׁ֛ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים י֖וֹם יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃

Joab gave the king the total from the registration of the people: in Israel there were eight hundred thousand valiant men who could draw the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand.[^6]
וַיִּתֵּ֥ן יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת־מִסְפַּ֥ר מִפְקַד־הָעָ֖ם אֶל־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַתְּהִ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל שְׁמֹנֶה֩ מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֤לֶף אִֽישׁ־חַ֙יִל֙ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֔רֶב וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה חֲמֵשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

But David's conscience troubled him[^7] after he had counted the people. David said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, LORD, please take away the guilt of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."

וַיַּ֤ךְ לֵב־דָּוִד֙ אֹת֔וֹ אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֖ן סָפַ֣ר אֶת־הָעָ֑ם ס וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה חָטָ֤אתִי מְאֹד֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי וְעַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה הַֽעֲבֶר־נָא֙ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֥י נִסְכַּ֖לְתִּי מְאֹֽד׃
When David got up in the morning, the word of the LORD had come to the prophet Gad, David's seer:
וַיָּ֥קָם דָּוִ֖ד בַּבֹּ֑קֶר פ וּדְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה הָיָה֙ אֶל־גָּ֣ד הַנָּבִ֔יא חֹזֵ֥ה דָוִ֖ד לֵאמֹֽר׃
"Go and tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am setting[^8] three things before you. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"
הָל֞וֹךְ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׁלֹ֕שׁ אָנֹכִ֖י נוֹטֵ֣ל עָלֶ֑יךָ בְּחַר־לְךָ֥ אַֽחַת־מֵהֶ֖ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּֽךְ׃

So Gad came to David and told him. He said to him, "Shall seven years[^9] of famine come upon you in your land? Or shall you flee for three months before your enemies while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of plague in your land? Now consider and decide what answer I should take back to the one who sent me."

וַיָּבֹא־גָ֥ד אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד וַיַּגֶּד־ל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֡וֹ הֲתָב֣וֹא לְךָ֣ שֶֽׁבַע־שָׁנִ֣ים ׀ רָעָ֣ב ׀ בְּאַרְצֶ֡ךָ אִם־שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳ֠דָשִׁים נֻסְךָ֨ לִפְנֵֽי־צָרֶ֜יךָ וְה֣וּא רֹדְפֶ֗ךָ וְאִם־הֱ֠יוֹת שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֥ים דֶּ֙בֶר֙ בְּאַרְצֶ֔ךָ עַתָּה֙ דַּ֣ע וּרְאֵ֔ה מָה־אָשִׁ֥יב שֹׁלְחִ֖י דָּבָֽר׃ ס
David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for his mercy is great, but do not let me fall into human hands."
וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־גָּ֖ד צַר־לִ֣י מְאֹ֑ד נִפְּלָה־נָּ֤א בְיַד־יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־רַבִּ֣ים *רחמו **רַֽחֲמָ֔יו וּבְיַד־אָדָ֖ם אַל־אֶפֹּֽלָה׃
So the LORD sent a plague on Israel from the morning until the appointed time,[^10] and seventy thousand of the people died, from Dan to Beersheba.
וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה דֶּ֙בֶר֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵהַבֹּ֖קֶר וְעַד־עֵ֣ת מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיָּ֣מָת מִן־הָעָ֗ם מִדָּן֙ וְעַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

When the angel[^11] stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD relented concerning the disaster[^12] and said to the angel who was destroying the people, "Enough! Now hold back your hand." The angel of the LORD was then by the threshing floor of Araunah[^13] the Jebusite.

וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ יָד֨וֹ הַמַּלְאָ֥ךְ ׀ יְרֽוּשָׁלַ[c]ם֮ לְשַׁחֲתָהּ֒ וַיִּנָּ֤חֶם יְהוָה֙ אֶל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וַ֠יֹּאמֶר לַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ הַמַּשְׁחִ֤ית בָּעָם֙ רַ֔ב עַתָּ֖ה הֶ֣רֶף יָדֶ֑ךָ וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ הָיָ֔ה עִם־גֹּ֖רֶן *האורנה **הָאֲרַ֥וְנָה הַיְבֻסִֽי׃ ס

When David saw the angel who was striking down the people, he said to the LORD, "I am the one who has sinned; I am the one who has done wrong.[^14] But these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand be against me and against my father's house."

וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶל־יְהוָ֜ה בִּרְאֹת֣וֹ ׀ אֶֽת־הַמַּלְאָ֣ךְ ׀ הַמַּכֶּ֣ה בָעָ֗ם וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֤י חָטָ֙אתִי֙ וְאָנֹכִ֣י הֶעֱוֵ֔יתִי וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַצֹּ֖אן מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א יָדְךָ֛ בִּ֖י וּבְבֵ֥ית אָבִֽי׃ פ
That day Gad came to David and said to him, "Go up and set up an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah[^15] the Jebusite."
וַיָּבֹא־גָ֥ד אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ עֲלֵה֙ הָקֵ֤ם לַֽיהוָה֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּגֹ֖רֶן *ארניה **אֲרַ֥וְנָה הַיְבֻסִֽי׃
So David went up at Gad's word, as the LORD had commanded.
וַיַּ֤עַל דָּוִד֙ כִּדְבַר־גָּ֔ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָֽה׃
When Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants coming over toward him, Araunah went out and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.
וַיַּשְׁקֵ֣ף אֲרַ֗וְנָה וַיַּ֤רְא אֶת־הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְאֶת־עֲבָדָ֔יו עֹבְרִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֲרַ֔וְנָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אַפָּ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃
Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague may be held back from the people."
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲרַ֔וְנָה מַדּ֛וּעַ בָּ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־עַבְדּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד לִקְנ֧וֹת מֵעִמְּךָ֣ אֶת־הַגֹּ֗רֶן לִבְנ֤וֹת מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְתֵעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל הָעָֽם׃

Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take it and offer up whatever seems good to him. Look, here are the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the oxen's yokes[^16] for the wood.
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲרַ֙וְנָה֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד יִקַּ֥ח וְיַ֛עַל אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַטּ֣וֹב *בעינו **בְּעֵינָ֑יו רְאֵה֙ הַבָּקָ֣ר לָעֹלָ֔ה וְהַמֹּרִגִּ֛ים וּכְלֵ֥י הַבָּקָ֖ר לָעֵצִֽים׃
All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king."[^17] And Araunah said to the king, "May the LORD your God accept you."
הַכֹּ֗ל נָתַ֛ן אֲרַ֥וְנָה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ ס וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲרַ֙וְנָה֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יִרְצֶֽךָ׃

But the king said to Araunah, "No, I will buy it from you for a price. I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels[^18] of silver.

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־אֲרַ֗וְנָה לֹ֚א כִּֽי־קָנ֨וֹ אֶקְנֶ֤ה מֵאֽוֹתְךָ֙ בִּמְחִ֔יר וְלֹ֧א אַעֲלֶ֛ה לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהַ֖י עֹל֣וֹת חִנָּ֑ם וַיִּ֨קֶן דָּוִ֤ד אֶת־הַגֹּ֙רֶן֙ וְאֶת־הַבָּקָ֔ר בְּכֶ֖סֶף שְׁקָלִ֥ים חֲמִשִּֽׁים׃
David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings.[^19] Then the LORD answered prayers for the land, and the plague was held back from Israel.[^20]
וַיִּבֶן֩ שָׁ֨ם דָּוִ֤ד מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַל עֹל֖וֹת וּשְׁלָמִ֑ים וַיֵּעָתֵ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ וַתֵּעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: 1 Chronicles 21:1 reads "Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to count Israel."
n.3: Probably the Arnon valley.
n.4: Hebrew *tachtim chodshi*, an unexplained name. Some manuscripts of the Septuagint read "the land of the Hittites, to Kadesh".
n.5: Hebrew *Danah ya'an*. The meaning is uncertain: perhaps "Dan and Ijon", or simply Dan.
n.6: 1 Chronicles 21:5 gives 1,100,000 for Israel and 470,000 for Judah.
n.7: Literally "David's heart struck him".
n.8: Hebrew *notel*, "lay upon", perhaps "impose". 1 Chronicles 21:10 has "offer".
n.9: 1 Chronicles 21:12 and the Septuagint read "three years".
n.10: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain: perhaps the end of the set time of three days, or the time of the evening sacrifice.
n.11: Or "the messenger". Hebrew *mal'akh* means both. Also in verse 17.
n.12: Or "changed his mind about the disaster".
n.13: The Hebrew text is written *ha-ornah* but read *ha-aravnah*, "Araunah". 1 Chronicles 21:15 calls him Ornan.
n.14: The Septuagint reads "and I, the shepherd, have done wrong".
n.15: The Hebrew text is written "Araniah" but read "Araunah".
n.17: Literally "The whole, Araunah the king gave to the king." Some take it to mean that Araunah had been the Jebusite king of Jerusalem.
n.18: A shekel is about ⅖ ounce (11.5 grams), so fifty shekels is about 1¼ pounds (575 grams). In 1 Chronicles 21:25 David pays six hundred shekels of gold for the site.
n.20: The Septuagint adds "And Solomon later added to the altar, for it was small at first."
